claims.title: Foundation of the Mali Empire on the upper Niger
claims.summary: Sundiata Keita unites the Malinké chiefdoms of the Manding heartland and founds the Mali Empire, with its capital at Niani on the upper Niger.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1235-foundation-of-the-mali-empire-on-the-upper-niger, claim TL:GIN:event:1235:foundation-of-the-mali-empire-on-the-upper-niger, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage makes Mali's gold legendary
claims.summary: Under Mansa Musa, the Mali Empire — embracing the Mande lands of the upper Niger — reaches its height and becomes renowned abroad for the wealth of its rulers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1324-mansa-musa-s-pilgrimage-makes-mali-s-gold, claim TL:GIN:event:1324:mansa-musa-s-pilgrimage-makes-mali-s-gold, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Songhai ascendancy in the western Sudan
claims.summary: Askia Muhammad seizes power and expands the Songhai Empire, which dominates much of the Niger valley and the western Sudan into the sixteenth century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1493-songhai-ascendancy-in-the-western-sudan, claim TL:GIN:event:1493:songhai-ascendancy-in-the-western-sudan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Songhai to a Moroccan army
claims.summary: A Moroccan expeditionary force defeats the Songhai at Tondibi, ending the era of the great Sahelian empires that had embraced the Guinea region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1591-fall-of-songhai-to-a-moroccan-army, claim TL:GIN:event:1591:fall-of-songhai-to-a-moroccan-army, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fulani jihad founds the Imamate of Futa Jallon
claims.summary: Fulani pastoralists and Muslim traders rise against the non-Muslim chiefdoms of the Futa Jallon highlands, founding an Islamic theocratic state governed by sharia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1725-fulani-jihad-founds-the-imamate-of-futa-jallon, claim TL:GIN:event:1725:fulani-jihad-founds-the-imamate-of-futa-jallon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ibrahima Sori succeeds Karamokho Alfa
claims.summary: On the death of the first leader Karamokho Alfa, the military commander Ibrahima Sori takes power and consolidates the imamate as a regional force.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1751-ibrahima-sori-succeeds-karamokho-alfa, claim TL:GIN:event:1751:ibrahima-sori-succeeds-karamokho-alfa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French annexation of Futa Jallon
claims.summary: After decades of nominal autonomy, the imamate is brought under French colonial control as European expansion absorbs the Guinea interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1896-french-annexation-of-futa-jallon, claim TL:GIN:event:1896:french-annexation-of-futa-jallon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Samori proclaims the Wassoulou Empire
claims.summary: Samori Touré declares himself faama of the Wassoulou Empire, the state he has built in the savannas of present-day Upper Guinea and beyond.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1878-samori-proclaims-the-wassoulou-empire, claim TL:GIN:event:1878:samori-proclaims-the-wassoulou-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Kankan
claims.summary: Samori takes control of the major Dyula trading centre of Kankan on the upper Milo, a hub of the kola-nut trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1881-capture-of-kankan, claim TL:GIN:event:1881:capture-of-kankan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islam proclaimed state religion; Samori takes the title almami
claims.summary: Samori formally adopts Islam as the religion of his empire and assumes the title of almami, fusing political and religious authority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1884-islam-proclaimed-state-religion-samori-takes, claim TL:GIN:event:1884:islam-proclaimed-state-religion-samori-takes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaties with France
claims.summary: Samori signs agreements with France, including the Treaty of Bissandougou in 1887, as he manoeuvres between negotiation and war against colonial expansion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1887-treaties-with-france, claim TL:GIN:event:1887:treaties-with-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Samori Touré
claims.summary: After nearly two decades of resistance and a long fighting retreat eastward, Samori is captured by French forces at Guélémou and later exiled to Gabon, where he dies in 1900.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1898-capture-of-samori-toure, claim TL:GIN:event:1898:capture-of-samori-toure, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Conakry
claims.summary: The French establish Conakry on the Atlantic coast; it becomes the capital of the colony of French Guinea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1884-founding-of-conakry, claim TL:GIN:event:1884:founding-of-conakry, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of French Guinea established
claims.summary: The coastal territory of Rivières du Sud is reorganised into the colony of French Guinea, its borders extended over the conquered interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1891-colony-of-french-guinea-established, claim TL:GIN:event:1891:colony-of-french-guinea-established, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Incorporation into French West Africa
claims.summary: French Guinea becomes a constituent colony of the federation of French West Africa, administered from Dakar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1895-incorporation-into-french-west-africa, claim TL:GIN:event:1895:incorporation-into-french-west-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Parti Démocratique de Guinée
claims.summary: Postwar political mobilisation gives rise to the PDG, which under Ahmed Sékou Touré becomes the leading nationalist party in the colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1947-rise-of-the-parti-democratique-de-guinee, claim TL:GIN:event:1947:rise-of-the-parti-democratique-de-guinee, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Guinea votes 'Non'
claims.summary: In the constitutional referendum, Guinea overwhelmingly rejects de Gaulle's French Community — the only French African colony to do so.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1958-guinea-votes-non, claim TL:GIN:event:1958:guinea-votes-non, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence proclaimed
claims.summary: Days after France abruptly withdraws its aid and personnel, Guinea proclaims itself a sovereign republic with Ahmed Sékou Touré as president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1958-independence-proclaimed, claim TL:GIN:event:1958:independence-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Camp Boiro and the one-party state
claims.summary: Under a one-party socialist regime, the Camp Boiro detention centre becomes the centre of a repression in which thousands of detainees are executed or die from torture and starvation.

sources.label: Guinea plans a Truth Commission (on Camp Boiro)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1960-camp-boiro-and-the-one-party-state, claim TL:GIN:event:1960:camp-boiro-and-the-one-party-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Sékou Touré
claims.summary: President Sékou Touré dies while receiving medical treatment abroad, ending more than a quarter-century of one-party rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1984-death-of-sekou-toure, claim TL:GIN:event:1984:death-of-sekou-toure, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lansana Conté seizes power
claims.summary: A bloodless military coup led by Colonel Lansana Conté takes control after Sékou Touré's death; political prisoners at Camp Boiro are released.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-1984-lansana-conte-seizes-power, claim TL:GIN:event:1984:lansana-conte-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Camara's coup after Conté's death
claims.summary: On the death of long-ruling President Lansana Conté, Captain Moussa Dadis Camara leads a military junta to power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-2008-camara-s-coup-after-conte-s-death, claim TL:GIN:event:2008:camara-s-coup-after-conte-s-death, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conakry stadium massacre
claims.summary: Security forces fire on a peaceful opposition rally in a Conakry stadium, killing at least 157 people and committing widespread sexual violence.

sources.label: Guinea: Ex-Coup Leader Charged in 2009 Massacre

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-2009-conakry-stadium-massacre, claim TL:GIN:event:2009:conakry-stadium-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alpha Condé elected; return to civilian rule
claims.summary: Veteran opposition leader Alpha Condé wins Guinea's first competitive presidential election, beginning a civilian government; he is re-elected in 2015 and 2020.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-2010-alpha-conde-elected-return-to-civilian-rule, claim TL:GIN:event:2010:alpha-conde-elected-return-to-civilian-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Doumbouya's coup ousts Condé
claims.summary: Special-forces commander Mamady Doumbouya overthrows President Alpha Condé, dissolves the constitution and installs himself as transitional leader.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Guinea: From the heartland of the Mande to the bauxite republic", terralore.co/country/GIN/chronicle#ev-2021-doumbouya-s-coup-ousts-conde, claim TL:GIN:event:2021:doumbouya-s-coup-ousts-conde, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
